candidate: gemma4_warp_tree2: interleave the two keys' pass-1 shuffle trees level by level
reason: neutral at sliding and slower at full, so it was reverted. It also corrects iteration 24's reading of the tree: the cost is block-level SIMD-pipe throughput, not a serialised chain, which is why interleaving cannot help and why adding warps (1024 threads) did not help either.

mechanism.hypothesis: the two keys per tile interleave their K loads and dot products but then run two back-to-back 5-level shuffle chains of 40 shuffles each, so the second tree waits on the first; interleaving the levels gives the warp two independent chains to overlap
mechanism.why_it_failed: 1024 keys x 40 shuffles x 16 warps = 655k shuffles in the 108 us iteration 24 measured, i.e. ~5 cycles per shuffle per warp, which is the block's 16 warps saturating its 4 SIMD pipes. Both calls are inlined and independent, so the scheduler had already overlapped them; the chain was never the limiter.
mechanism.corrected_diagnosis: pass 1's tree is block-level pipe-throughput bound. The structural limiter is the grid: gemma4_attention_decode_launch sets grid = tokens * num_heads, so a decode step launches 16 blocks of 512 threads on a 96-CU GPU.
mechanism.next_candidate: split-K: divide each head's key range across N blocks and combine their (max, denominator, weighted-V) partials with an online-softmax rescale. Changed arithmetic, so it needs the docs/EXECUTION-PROFILES.md production-profile gate via scripts/gemma4_teacher_forced_gate.py rather than parity, and its payoff is occupancy rather than removed work.
